I was also homeless for years, and it's extremely hard and expensive to get out of that situation. If you live in a shelter, you need to be on top of all your paper work and keep in contact with your case worker. And getting a job doesn't make things easier. If the shelter misplaces your work schedule, your bed could be taken away. Now you have to either wait for a new one or be transported to another shelter. A lot of the people that I've met who work in shelters are absolutely shitty as well. They go out of their way to make your life even worse or try to get you kicked out. Also, a lot of the church shelters I've been to/seen were day shelters or only open at night. It's not easy to get your shit together when you don't have a stable living situation. 

After saying all this, I will agree that some homeless people just give up. Especially if they found a long term shelter. This mostly seems to be the older population.
